## Step 1 execution notes (2026-11-09)
Step 1 is merged into `restructure/integration` (be-s0 `8be7848a`, fe-s1 `b40c8c81`) and re-gated, and the first HOST checkpoint passed. Full record: [step-logs/step1.md](step-logs/step1.md). Two plan fixes came from the S1 agent, and the coordinator checked both against the S1 baselines:

| # | Change |
|---|---|
| S1-a | **Baseline keys follow moves.** `boundary-baseline.json` and `size-baseline.json` are keyed by file path, so every step that moves client files renames the moved files' keys in both files to the new paths, with the same counts, in the same commit. Otherwise the old key goes stale, the moved file counts as a new file with violations, and `npm test` fails. This is in frontend.md §3 ("Baseline keys" detail, new C1 detail) and in the A1, A2, A3, B1, B2 and C1 briefs, and §5.2 points to it. **B2 was added** to the requested list (A1, A2, A3, B1, C1) because it moves `media-tags/rules/media-language.ts`, which has a `size-baseline.json` entry (903 lines). `generated-markers-baseline.json` is keyed by base name, so moves don't affect it. |
| S1-b | **C4 strict mode needs the platform hosts.** As written, rule 4 allows the raw global only in `host/context.ts`, `features/*/host*.ts` and `bootstrap/**`. But all eight core hosts that stay in `host/` (core, api, dom, navigation, session, ui, admin-config, bootstrap-pages) and `core/lifecycle-entry.ts` read it: each has a `raw-global JellyfinEnhanced` entry in the S1 baseline, and no step converts them. **Decision:** they are platform, not features, so rule 4's allowlist includes them. This is written into §2.4 rule 4, the C4 table row and brief (which adds them to `globalAllowed` in `scan.mjs`), and §5.2. |
| S1-c | **Open, not decided:** two more S1-baseline entries are outside every C1–C3 step, so strict C4 still can't pass with them: `host/bootstrap-pages-host.ts` has 3 rule-2 `host-import`s (type imports from `features/{calendar,downloads,seerr/recommendations}/types.ts`), and `admin/config/page/media-tags-tab.ts` has 2 rule-3 internals reads. The C4 brief now says to stop and report if they are still present, and not to allowlist them. |
| S1-d | **HOST procedure note (no plan edit).** `je up … --image jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4` created the server, but its deploy build failed for two reasons. It builds a clean `HEAD` clone with no `node_modules`, so `Directory.Build.targets`' client check fails. And `je deploy` builds with `-warnaserror`, while this tree has the one baselined CS8604 warning. So the jf12 plugin was built from the merged tree with a plain `dotnet build -c Release -p:JellyfinTarget=jf12`, and installed the way `je deploy` installs it (DLL plus the skill's `meta.json`). Later HOST checkpoints should do the same until the baselined warning is gone. |

## Step 2 execution notes (2026-11-09)
Step 2 ran as **A0 → A1 → A2 → A3** on `restructure/fe-a` (record: [step-logs/step2.md](step-logs/step2.md)). The first attempt stopped before committing: simulated on the S1 tree, A1–A3 created new cross-feature pairs (A1 2, A2 19, A3 21 new `(file, key)` pairs), because the moved panels' imports of settings-panel `context.ts`, `dom.ts`, `registry.ts` and `settings-values.ts`, registry.ts's imports of the moved panels, and the moved admin host's imports of `settings-panel/registry.ts` and `host/settings-host.ts` all become edges between features. **Coordinator decision (final):** keep the ratchet strict. Never add a baseline entry and never widen a rule; the only re-key allowed is the relocation of an existing violation (same edge, same count, new path).

| # | Change |
|---|---|
| S2-a | **New prep step A0** (frontend.md §3 table and "A0" detail, §6 brief). `git mv` settings-panel/`dom.ts` and `settings-values.ts` → `features/shared/`; types-only `settings-panel/public-api.ts` (`PanelContext`, `SearchHit`, `EnhancedUi`, `MediaTagsHubApi`) and `media-tags/public-api.ts` (the tag panels' registry types; until A2 re-exported via settings-panel's public API); `registry.ts` takes those types from `media-tags/public-api.ts`; new `host/context.ts` re-exports `SaveOptions`/`SettingsDocument` (type-only) for the admin host. Rule 1 already allows `import type`/`export type … from` of another feature's `public-api.ts`, so no rule changed. Built JS changed only in `// client/src/` comments and maps. |
| S2-b | **Baseline keys cover target paths.** A move renames the moved file's keys **and** every occurrence of its path as a target inside other entries, with the same counts; pairs that become legal are lowered in the same commit. The §3 check command now greps `<old path>"`, which catches both forms (the old `"<old path>"` pattern missed target keys). |
| S2-c | **Cross-feature moves make their edges legal first**, never record new ones (§3). Simulate the move in a throwaway worktree before committing. |
| S2-d | **C1 owns `host/settings-panel-host.ts` → `settings-panel/host.ts`** (§1a, §3 table, A3 and C1 briefs); A3 leaves it. C1 also has two known edges to handle (§3 "C1 (host moves)"): move the `SaveOptions`/`SettingsDocument` declarations into `host/context.ts` before moving `host/settings-host.ts`, and re-key the moved panels' runtime imports of the settings-panel host. |
| S2-e | **Results.** No new boundary pair at any step. `boundary-baseline.json` fell from 536 violations (420 pairs, 292 files) to 502 (386 pairs, 278 files): A2 lowered 8 pairs that became same-feature imports, A3 lowered 26 (the admin files' imports of their host, the moved host's host-imports and its raw-global read). `size-baseline.json` is unchanged in total (22 files, 25,608 lines; 7 keys renamed). C2 extends `host/context.ts`; S2 extends the two existing public-api files. |
